summary.headline: Archean Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 14% YoY to INR3,321m and EBITDA margin expanded to 25.3%, but logistics costs and Hajipir road works kept salt volumes down 12%.

segments.name: Bromine
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,333 million, +58% YoY on 4,175 tons; realizations up 50% YoY and expected to hold near INR300/kg. Production up 7% YoY despite lower GPL; about 3 days lost to grid power cuts and planned maintenance.

segments.name: Industrial salt
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,713 million on 982,000 tons, down 12% YoY. Dispatches hit by vessel shortages, diesel shortages and order deferrals; finished goods inventory rose. Realizations broadly flat QoQ.

segments.name: Bromine derivatives (Acume Chemicals)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR300 million, +28.1% YoY; EBITDA INR19 million vs loss of INR27 million a year ago, first positive EBITDA. Loss before tax narrowed to INR58.6 million from INR103.3 million. Capacity utilisation about 40%.

segments.name: Sulphate of potash (SOP)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR113 million vs INR35 million for full FY26. Sales of 1,952 tons at about INR58,000/ton. Phase 1 trials completed June 2026; Phase 2 targeted by end-Q3 FY27 (also referred to as December 2026).

segments.name: Oilfield chemicals (Idealis)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR3.5 million with EBITDA loss of INR13.4 million; business still in investment phase ahead of plant readiness and customer trials.

segments.name: Neun and SiCSem (consolidated)
segments.commentary: Combined revenue INR0.4 million and EBITDA loss INR5.6 million; investment phase.

qa_highlights.question: Why was bromine volume 4,175 tons vs ~4,500 implied by 55 tpd run rate, and is the 20,000-ton FY27 target intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 325 tons short: about 200 tons lost to grid power cuts (3-3.5 days) and about 150 tons to planned shutdowns; exit run rate of 20,000-25,000 tons still the target, with Q2 and Q3 the real test.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for bromine realisations over next 3-4 quarters given contract structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is fairly confident of holding the weighted average blend; long-term contracts are 60-70% of volume, spot 30-35%, and some spot impact expected.

qa_highlights.question: Salt shipments shortfall and whether demand or logistics is the issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand has not moved backwards; the shortfall reflects QVC deferrals and logistics issues including vessel slots and cut-offs; Kandla added as third port from Q2 to reduce blank sailings.

qa_highlights.question: How much cost saving if diesel and routes normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide numerically; said other expenses rose about INR40 crore YoY, ~60% from logistics (mainly distance) and ~40% from diesel, with normalisation expected to reflect from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why are derivative prices up only ~10% vs bromine ~25%, and status of Gujarat lease?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the numbers quoted were not accurate, bromine is 40-50% of derivative cost so pass-through is fractional; lease closure expected in coming months, rents being paid and accepted.

qa_highlights.question: Timelines for zinc bromide and off-grid scale-up, and SiCSem timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Off-grid pilot needs several months to prove out; megawatt-plus plants in India not timed. SiCSem 24-27 months to commercial SOP from FSA; construction from late Aug/early Sep 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why has bromine volume been flat for five years versus capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited structural changes in brine feedstock needing recovery-system redesign, plus cyclonic rainfall in Kutch (average rainfall up to ~900 mm); 40,000-ton expansion timed to FY28-FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Demand outlook for oilfield chemicals and timing of volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Indian drilling demand is small and most demand is overseas; pack and starch (Nagri) volumes expected H2 FY27, bentonite and barite (Mandvi) by end FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Semicon capex phasing?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Kumar said 15-20% of USD249 million already spent, 60-65% in FY27 and 40-45% in FY28.

guidance_outlook: Bromine: exit FY27 at a 20,000-25,000 ton annual run rate (about 4,500 tons per quarter); FY28 full-year target about 25,000 tons per management's reply to DSP.
Industrial salt: volumes to normalise from Q3 FY27 once Hajipir-Jakhau/Mundra/Kandla highway works finish (guided end-September); double-digit salt growth expected from Q3 onwards.
SOP: full-year FY27 target of 9,000-10,000 tons; SOP scale-up to be completed by end of this year.
Derivatives to continue to build on break-even; utilisation and mix to lift contribution margins.
Semiconductor (SiCSem): 24-27 months to commercial start of production from FSA signing (11 May 2026); construction to start late August/early September 2026.
Capex: SiCSem capex USD249 million; 15-20% incurred, 60-65% in FY27, 40-45% in FY28.
Brine field phase one commissioning may be pre-poned to after monsoon; Gujarat lease extension expected to close in coming months.
capex_capacity: Bromine capacity about 43,000 tons per analyst; management says ~40,000 tons with 25,000 tons run rate achievable via debottlenecking; 40,000 tons needs further investment timed with flame retardant project and expansion, likely FY28-FY29 decision in H2 FY28.
Brine field expansion: most of phase one complete; commissioning possibly postponed to post-monsoon; land lease extension with Gujarat government under discussion.
SiCSem (USD249 million capex) in execution; environmental clearance and consent to establish pending; general contractor onboarded.
Gujarat plant (Idealis) production-ready, awaiting state approvals; Nagri (Andhra Pradesh) starch and pack products in customer trials.
Kandla stockyard built; shipments from Kandla to start Q2 FY27, expanding from two to three ports.
Off-grid energy labs: 10 MWh zinc bromide battery pilot inaugurated at Hook, UK; management says Jhagadia zinc bromide REACH certification nearly complete.
demand_pricing: Bromine demand firm across most geographies; supply imbalance of prior two quarters normalised and pricing corrected; landed prices in China down 30-40% in 12 weeks. Contracts: 60-70% long-term, 30-35% spot.

Industrial salt pricing stabilised after FY26 declines; Q1 realisations broadly flat; competition high from new capacity in Australia and elsewhere. Chlor-alkali demand positive but PVC demand hit by conflict.
QVC (salt customer) still on hold due to Middle East conflict; oil and gas derivative offtake volatile. 60-70% of salt volume on customer-nominated vessels, causing delays and blank sailings.
Sea freight up 30-35%; HSD diesel up nearly 60% YoY in April-June, normalised in July. Road distance from Jakhau roughly doubled to 500+ km.
Bromine derivatives: product mix shift (NPBR volumes ~350 tons in Q1 vs 25-30 tons a year ago), sodium bromide stopped, cost savings at Jhagadia.
risks_watch: Logistics: Hajipir road works due end-September; any slip extends salt volume decline and freight costs; diesel prices and sea freight (up 30-35%) remain elevated.
Bromine volume recovery: power cuts, planned shutdowns, sulphur and coal cost inflation and need for recovery improvements to reach 4,500 tons/quarter.
Bromine pricing: China landed prices down 30-40%; spot share 30-35% exposed to correction.
Salt demand: QVC on hold due to Middle East conflict; customer order deferrals and commercial discipline may affect conversion.
Gujarat brine lease extension not yet closed; brine phase one commissioning timing.
SiCSem and off-grid execution: environmental clearance pending; pilot performance not yet proven; Idealis and SOP feedstock sourcing still challenging.
Q2 and Q3 FY27 volumes are the key test; Q2 expected to be weaker on monsoon-related schedules.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously confident: management highlighted sequential margin gains and derivatives break-even but repeatedly attributed the YoY salt volume and profit decline to temporary logistics, fuel and power factors, and pushed key tests to Q2 and Q3 FY27. Management declined to quantify cost savings and deferred some questions to the IR team.

adds.what: SiCSem semiconductor plant (USD249m capex), commercial production 24-27 months from FSA signing
Bromine run-rate exit at 20,000-25,000 t/yr via debottlenecking (about 4,500 t/qtr)
SOP scale-up to complete by end of FY27 (Phase 2), 9,000-10,000 t FY27 sales target
Brine field phase one commissioning, possibly post-monsoon
Idealis Gujarat plant, production-ready awaiting state approvals
Kandla stockyard, shipments from Kandla starting Q2 FY27

growth.why: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 14% YoY, with bromine up 58% and SOP ramping toward 9,000-10,000 t, but salt volumes fell 12% and management guides salt growth only from Q3 after highway works; SiCSem and bromine expansions are a 2-6 quarter horizon.
